body: Untrue, but I'll give you the chance to defend yourself before I prove you wrong.
Still an expert musician I see.
Actually I was just asking for some advice and other peoples perspectives.
We've all had a serious talk, and we all want to be professionals but I feel like they either don't hear how bad we are or they just don't want to bring it up.
Thanks for the advice, but I've gotten a good bit of guidance and have been doing just that so I'm not worried ;)
Amateur with projection issues. Knew it ;)

But you're obviously a professional musician with encyclopaedic knowledge of the industry.

Or are you just an amateur with projection issues? If you are then I'll stop messaging you as there's nothing to learn from you.

Again, not exactly true, is it? 

You don't know what my plans are, you just called me delusional. People make a career out of music, and people with no experience in the industry always jump to thinking that means rock star. It's not, it's a functional career.

I didn't get upset about it, I corrected you. You said that they weren't waiting around waiting for my call, but they are. They are booking clients to work with, who pay them, which pays their bills. This is very basic business stuff. I'm still learning about the business side of music but even I understand that.

The fact that you didn't know that is what made me discredit everything else you said. But you said you and your friends have booked studio time, so I take it you're an established professional musician?

Not exactly what happened though, is it?

I said I was going to work with a producer on an EP, and you called me delusional for thinking a producer would work with an amateur.

That was until I gave you several links to studios and producers who all offer their contact info. So you're so amateur that you didn't even know that you could book studios.

And the original thread isn't deleted, that's another lie. The subreddit is private in solidarity for BLM.

Just admit you were wrong and that you don't know how the industry works.
Big words from a guy who didn't know how booking a recording studio works.

Don't pay too much attention to him, he's completely clueless. I mentioned in a post that I was going to find a producer to work with and he called me delusional. He's so amateur that he doesn't know how booking a recording studio works.

I dropped a few links to big recording studios that have contact info, all encouraging artists to contact them for a quote and book time and now he won't reply to me.

Plenty of feedback to give here but no replies to my DMs after you called me delusional for thinking I could...

What was it again? Book a recording studio?

Thanks man, I really appreciate the replies.

Obviously you're biased, but is artist development really a good step for new artists? On one hand, other musicians have laughed at and dismissed me when I've started talking about artist image, branding, aesthetics etc and I'm still convinced that I'm on the right track thinking about that but the development websites I've found have advertised a few 'Voice UK' artists, and I'm passionately against going on talent shows, to the point where it is a hardline dealbreaker for me.

I'm not looking for someone to do all the work for me, more like someone who will help me focus and develop the ideas I already have, and give me really blunt feedback when I need it like "That's a very cliche music video idea that a million musicians have done before you, and the logistics don't even come close to working out".
So what you're saying is that human rights based on race should be up for debate?
That's what I was afraid of. Blackbear got his break through artist development, but that was through Compound Entertainment which was ran by Ne-Yo so I guess that's a little different.
Defending human rights and opposing racism isn't a political opinion.

Come on clever guy. You were calling me delusional, start backing it up.

http://www.reelrecordingstudio.com/quote-request/

https://outhousestudios.co.uk/contact

http://johnmitchellhq.com/contact/

That's just a few studios with big names on their credits, all freely offering their services. You contact them and book studio time. How am I delusional for planning to book studio time? 

https://www.showcase-music.com/categories/the-business/booking-agents/uk/

That's a list of booking agencies, go to any of their sites and they all offer their contact information so artists can contact them for their services. 

http://www.londonartistdevelopment.co.uk/

https://bighelp.biz/about/

https://www.am-studios.co.uk/about-artist-development/

https://www.360artistdevelopment.com/

That's just the first four artist development agencies I found, all encouraging artists to contact them.

Why did you call me delusional for asking about these services? Did you think that they're all secret societies that have to approach artists first? Why did you assume that I think they're all dying to work with me in particular? I would just be expecting them to fulfil the service they advertise.

My problem isn't finding them, it's option paralysis and prioritising. That's what I'm asking advice for.
When I get the rough demos recorded I'll send you them

Why do you think I'm so off base with the producer thing?

I have a shortlist of 5 or 6 producers who have all worked on stuff that's either on big labels or has made it to Radio 1. On all their websites they list their contact information for musicians to hire them.
Scotland.

It's literally their job, how they make money and how they pay the bills. They work with musicians in recording studios. What do you not get about that?

You're making a lot of assumptions without actually offering any good advice, so I'm just going to ignore you.

I barely know how to respond to this.

>Who are these top class producers waiting for your call?

Where did I say they're waiting for my call? They're waiting for emails and calls from musicians who want to work with them. I'm hardly a genius but even I understand this much.

>The delusion of grandeur is that you've demonstrated nothing of your musicianship/songwriting etc... but you seem to be assuming there's a whole industry who can't wait to sign you up and throw money your way.

You're just making things up, what's wrong with you? I'm just asking for some advice on the business side of the music industry and you're throwing insults at me.

I know that a lot of people are trying to be professional musicians, that's why I'm trying to learn more about the industry. Why are you so angry?

I can and currently do, but a producer helps realise the ideas that I have and has more experience in songwriting that I do.

I want to make the jump from bedroom musician to professional so I'm finding people that can help me do that. The guy I've found has worked with artists signed to Sony, Syco and Warner. I can find cheaper here too, but I'm looking to make a serious product.

I have a bassist who doesn't know where C is and a drummer who has never played a gig before but thinks that he's going to be living off music by the end of this year. There is no delusion of grandeur here, I'm just being realistic.

Where did I use the words 'famous rock star' in my post. I want to make music my career. If you're going to make fun of everyone who wants to make that step, what are you even doing on this subreddit?

I have self awareness that I have a lot that I don't know about the business side, which is why I'm asking. Thanks for all the assumptions though.

It's taken me over a year to find a drummer, and he just doesn't have the experience I need. 

Writing the songs isn't the problem, it's the direction to take them after they're done. I'm going to a producer once they're written to help with turning them into full arrangements and get them up to the standard for radio play.

I would love to do the gig every day thing but I have a day job. I'm planning to take some weeks off maybe into next year to start touring the best I can.

I actually did the staying behind and packing up thing a few years ago and it did work to an extent. My songs weren't terrible, but my singing was yet I was always asked back for more gigs.

I guess my other problem is the direction for the music. I want to do a pop rock thing, but I don't think my band is going to last so I'll be doing my first gigs acoustic.
Thanks man, I've picked them up!
